headline: Trump calls Iran confrontation 'not a war' / 'a minor military operation'
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Trump, quoted verbatim by ANI (T1 wire), Gulf News (T3), Times of India (T3), News18, Clash Report] 'Iran is not a war. It's a minor military operation.' 'We made a lot of progress with Iran.
sources: President Donald Trump, remarks to reporters, West Palm Beach, Nov 6 (on camera, C-SPAN footage via Roya News; AJ English reel)
fault_line: Is 'no American deaths in five months' the same as 'not a war' -- when US jets just bombed Qeshm, 11 ships were attacked in Hormuz this week, and 22 people were killed in Sanaa?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Trump, quoted verbatim by ANI (T1 wire), Gulf News (T3), Times of India (T3), News18, Clash Report] 'Iran is not a war. It's a minor military operation.' 'We made a lot of progress with Iran. We're taking out more oil now than we were before the war. It's not a war. It can't be a war when for five months nobody was hurt, killed, or anything else. It's not a war.' 'We haven't lost anybody in seven months.' Trump confirmed Friday's limited US strikes on Qeshm Island, saying US forces destroyed an Iranian anti-aircraft device 'in about 15 minutes, maybe five.' In a Truth Social post he claimed his intervention stopped Iran acquiring a nuclear weapon and is 'universally recognised yet deliberately underreported.' In a separate on-camera clip (AVA reel, Nov 7 06:43Z) he called the Hormuz blockade 'the greatest blockade in military history,' claiming 'nothing passes through without US approval and nothing is going to Iran.' The remarks follow the Republican midterm rout, which Trump and Vance publicly attribute in part to the war (ToI: Vance blamed the war for the defeat; fuel prices cited). [CONTEXT] 'Small potatoes' was Trump's September phrasing for the same conflict; the Nov 6 remarks escalate the downplaying. The claim sits directly against the NBC eight-week window for renewed major combat operations (recorded 1700-04) and Bessent's outreach to China.
sections.what_verified: ANI wire (T1) + Gulf News own liveblog (T3) + Times of India (T3) carry the identical quotes; News18 and Clash Report (no declared tier, attribution only) carry the same quotes.
sections.what_disputed: (1) The US itself bombed Qeshm Island on Friday (Trump confirmed; Tasnim reported two missiles; recorded 0400-01/0700-01) -- a strike is not 'not a war' by any ordinary measure. (2) CRS report updated Oct 20 describes the conflict as a period of continued, although reduced, military confrontation (Sunday Guardian live). (3) 'Nothing passes through' Hormuz is false on counted data: UKMTO's weekly report (recorded 1700-01) counted 170 outbound + 155 inbound transits in the week ending Nov 6, ~65% below pre-conflict -- reduced, not zero. (4) 'Nobody hurt or killed in five months': Gulf News itself notes the assertion 'has not been independently established'; the wider war has killed people this week alone -- 11 ships attacked in Hormuz with 3 sunk (UKMTO), 22 killed in Sanaa al-Shariya (1700-02), 30 killed in the Taiz market strike, 1,610 killed in Gaza since the ceasefire (1700-05). Trump appears to mean no AMERICAN deaths, but he did not say that. (5) Iran's IRGC spokesman Mohebbi claims 260 hostile aircraft downed (recorded 1700-03, unverified) -- the direct rebuttal to 'no losses.' (6) The 'taking out more oil' claim has no published volume figure behind it in any carrying outlet.
sections.why_matters: Trump says it's 'not a war' -- the same day his own military bombed Qeshm and 11 ships were attacked in Hormuz. Whose war is it then?
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP -- Trump calls Iran confrontation 'not a war' / 'a minor military operation': 'for five months nobody was hurt, killed'
